item.title: Clifford hierarchy
item.description: Clifford operations are the normalizers of the n-qubit Pauli group: GPG ^\dagger = \pm Q where G is a n-qubit Clifford operation and P,Q are Pauli operators.

item.title: Steane code
item.description: The Steane code is obtained by applying the CSS code procedure to the [7,4,3]-Hamming code.

item.title: Eastin-Knill theorem
item.description: The Eastin-Knill theorem states that, for any nontrivial local-error-detecting quantum code, the set of logical unitary product operators is not universal.

item.title: Code blocks
item.description: Consider a code that implements logical qubits in a certain way. We may then want to perform operations on those logical qubits.

item.title: Locality-preserving gates
item.description: Locality-preserving gates are a very useful class of fault-tolerant gates which are relatively easy to manipulate in practice.

item.title: Distance
item.description: The distance of a stabilizer code is given by the minimum number of “active” Pauli’s found in the set of logical errors.

item.title: Fault-tolerant logical gates
item.description: Fault-tolerant logical gates are a class of logical gates that don’t reduce the effective distance to O(1) when the class grows in physical size.

item.title: Transversal Gates
item.description: Transversal gates are the easiest example of locality-preserving gates.
